tasks.subject: Task 0: ExtractData composite primary key
tasks.description:
**Goal:** `ExtractData` uses `(dataset_id, extract_task_id, name)` as its primary key instead of an auto-generated `id`, with all existing read/write code paths (including the fetch-then-update rerun path) proven still correct.

**Files:**
- Modify: backend/analytics/models.py:149-182 (the ExtractData class)
- Create: backend/analytics/migrations/0023_extractdata_composite_pk.py
- Modify: backend/analytics/admin.py:51-60 (ExtractDataAdmin)
- Modify: backend/analytics/tests/test_models.py

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] ExtractData has no id column at the DB level
- [ ] (dataset_id, extract_task_id, name) is the actual PRIMARY KEY constraint at the DB level
- [ ] name is NOT NULL at the DB level
- [ ] ExtractDataAdmin no longer references the removed id field anywhere
- [ ] All existing tests in analytics.tests.test_processing, analytics.tests.test_merge, visualize.tests.test_data, and analytics.tests.test_models still pass unmodified -- in particular test_rerun_only_reprocesses_null_positions and test_rerun_results_count_is_not_inflated_by_overlapping_name in test_processing.py, which exercise the fetch-an-existing-row-then-.save() code path and are the concrete proof that Django's insert-vs-update determination still works correctly for a model with no auto field

**Verify:** sudo docker compose run --rm backend uv run python manage.py test analytics.tests.test_models analytics.tests.test_processing analytics.tests.test_merge visualize.tests.test_data -v 2

**Steps:** Read current ExtractData model and processing.py's save-pattern code; update model with CompositePrimaryKey (verify exact Django 5.2 API empirically -- first use in codebase); write hand-written migration (RunSQL: ALTER COLUMN name SET NOT NULL, DROP CONSTRAINT extract_data_pkey, ADD PRIMARY KEY (dataset_id, extract_task_id, name), DROP COLUMN id -- with state_operations for AlterField(name), RemoveField(id), AddField(pk=CompositePrimaryKey)); update ExtractDataAdmin (drop id references, use dataset_id/extract_task_id/name); add DB-level tests (composite PK columns, id column removed, name NOT NULL); run full regression suite paying special attention to the two rerun tests; commit.

```json:metadata
{"files": ["backend/analytics/models.py", "backend/analytics/migrations/0023_extractdata_composite_pk.py", "backend/analytics/admin.py", "backend/analytics/tests/test_models.py"], "verifyCommand": "sudo docker compose run --rm backend uv run python manage.py test analytics.tests.test_models analytics.tests.test_processing analytics.tests.test_merge visualize.tests.test_data -v 2", "acceptanceCriteria": ["id column removed from extract_data", "composite PK (dataset_id, extract_task_id, name) at DB level", "name NOT NULL", "admin updated", "rerun tests prove save() insert/update still correct"], "modelTier": "standard"}
```

tasks.subject: Task 1: extract_tasks resource_ids_hash generated column and index rebuild
tasks.description:
**Goal:** extract_tasks gains a stored generated column resource_ids_hash (hashtext(resource_ids::text)), and both resource_ids-keyed unique indexes are rebuilt to use it instead of the raw array, shrinking the largest single index in the schema.

**Files:**
- Modify: backend/analytics/models.py (ExtractTask class)
- Create: backend/analytics/migrations/0024_extracttask_resource_ids_hash.py
- Modify: backend/analytics/tests/test_models.py

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] resource_ids_hash exists as an integer column on extract_tasks, GENERATED ALWAYS ... STORED
- [ ] Inserting a row with a given resource_ids array automatically populates resource_ids_hash with hashtext(resource_ids::text) -- verified by direct comparison in a test
- [ ] extract_tasks_fm_po_resources_null_kwargs_idx is rebuilt on (dataset_id, fm_id, po_id, resource_ids_hash)
- [ ] extract_tasks_fm_po_resources_kwargs_hash_idx is rebuilt on (dataset_id, fm_id, po_id, resource_ids_hash, MD5(kwargs::text))
- [ ] Both indexes remain UNIQUE with the same partial WHERE conditions as before
- [ ] extract_tasks_pending_idx is untouched
- [ ] Total size of the two rebuilt indexes is smaller than before, verified by direct measurement against a realistic-scale synthetic dataset
- [ ] All existing tests in analytics.tests.test_build_extract_tasks still pass

**Verify:** sudo docker compose run --rm backend uv run python manage.py test analytics.tests.test_models analytics.tests.test_build_extract_tasks -v 2

**Steps:** Read current ExtractTask model and migration 0022; add resource_ids_hash = models.GeneratedField(expression=Func(Cast("resource_ids", output_field=TextField()), function="hashtext"), output_field=IntegerField(), db_persist=True) -- verify exact SQL produced empirically, first use in codebase; write hand-written migration (ADD COLUMN ... GENERATED ALWAYS AS (hashtext(resource_ids::text)) STORED, then DROP+CREATE both unique indexes on the hash column) with state_operations; add tests (column exists/generated, hash matches hashtext(), indexes use hash column); measure real size reduction against a synthetic ~5000-row/12-element-array dataset, report actual numbers; run tests; commit.

```json:metadata
{"files": ["backend/analytics/models.py", "backend/analytics/migrations/0024_extracttask_resource_ids_hash.py", "backend/analytics/tests/test_models.py"], "verifyCommand": "sudo docker compose run --rm backend uv run python manage.py test analytics.tests.test_models analytics.tests.test_build_extract_tasks -v 2", "acceptanceCriteria": ["resource_ids_hash generated column exists", "both unique indexes rebuilt on hash column", "pending_idx untouched", "measured size reduction reported", "build_extract_tasks tests pass"], "modelTier": "standard"}
```

tasks.subject: Task 2: Update views.py to query via the hash column
tasks.description:
**Goal:** RequestView.post's get-or-create loop filters on resource_ids_hash in addition to resource_ids, so Postgres actually uses the new smaller index for these lookups instead of falling back to a broader index-prefix-plus-heap-recheck scan.

**Files:**
- Modify: backend/analytics/views.py:217-259 (get-or-create loop)
- Modify: backend/analytics/tests/test_views.py (test_integrity_error_on_create_falls_back_to_get)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Both .get() calls and the .create() call filter/set resource_ids_hash alongside resource_ids (NOT on .create() -- generated columns reject explicit values on INSERT)
- [ ] The hash value is computed server-side by Postgres via a raw SQL expression (RawSQL("hashtext(%s::text)", [resource_ids])), not replicated in Python
- [ ] EXPLAIN on the .get() query shows an index scan using extract_tasks_fm_po_resources_null_kwargs_idx with all four columns as index conditions
- [ ] test_integrity_error_on_create_falls_back_to_get updated to match new call signature and still passes
- [ ] All other existing tests in test_views.py and test_ingest.py pass unmodified (ingest.py itself needs no code change)

**Verify:** sudo docker compose run --rm backend uv run python manage.py test analytics.tests.test_views analytics.tests.test_ingest -v 2

**Steps:** Read current views.py get-or-create block; add RawSQL("hashtext(%s::text)", [resource_ids]) filter to both .get() calls (import from django.db.models.expressions); verify empirically against real scratch DB that the RawSQL array-parameter formatting actually matches Postgres's own resource_ids::text cast (correctness-critical, not just an optimization -- a mismatch would cause DoesNotExist on rows that actually exist); verify via .explain() that the index is actually used; update the mocked test's expected call kwargs (may need to compare RawSQL params individually rather than dict-equality, verify empirically); run tests; commit.

```json:metadata
{"files": ["backend/analytics/views.py", "backend/analytics/tests/test_views.py"], "verifyCommand": "sudo docker compose run --rm backend uv run python manage.py test analytics.tests.test_views analytics.tests.test_ingest -v 2", "acceptanceCriteria": ["get-or-create filters on resource_ids_hash via server-side RawSQL", "create() does not set resource_ids_hash explicitly", "EXPLAIN confirms index scan on all 4 columns", "mocked test updated and passing", "ingest.py needs no change, confirmed via passing tests"], "modelTier": "standard"}
```

tasks.subject: Task 3: Deploy
tasks.description:
**USER-ORDERED GATE — NON-SKIPPABLE.** This task was requested by the user in the current conversation. It MUST NOT be closed by walking around it, by declaring it "verified inline", or by substituting a cheaper check. Close only after every item in acceptanceCriteria has been re-validated independently, with output captured.

**Goal:** Ship both schema changes to production via the existing CI/CD pipeline, with explicit attention to the fact that (unlike the original redesign's wipe-first deploy) both migrations run against live, non-empty, actively-written-to tables.

**Files:** none (deploy-only task)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Migrations 0023 and 0024 apply cleanly against production via the geoquery-db-migration Job
- [ ] extract_data confirmed to have no id column and the correct composite PK in production (direct information_schema query against the live DB)
- [ ] extract_tasks_fm_po_resources_null_kwargs_idx and extract_tasks_fm_po_resources_kwargs_hash_idx confirmed rebuilt on resource_ids_hash in production
- [ ] Real index size reduction measured and reported (before/after pg_total_relation_size comparison against production's actual current index sizes)
- [ ] A real on-demand request submission through RequestView.post succeeds end-to-end post-deploy
- [ ] processing-worker/background-worker/geoquery-import pods continue writing to extract_data without errors post-deploy

**Verify:** kubectl logs -n geoquery-prod job/geoquery-db-migration shows success; direct information_schema/pg_indexes queries against the live DB confirm both schema changes; no new errors in processing-worker/background-worker logs in the minutes following deploy

**Steps:** Pre-deploy sanity check (re-confirm 0 NULL names / 0 duplicate composite keys against CURRENT production data, since it's continuously growing -- STOP if either check fails); open PR, merge with [DEPLOY-X.Y.Z] marker, confirm resolved BACKEND_SHA matches the merge commit (per the PR #17 fix); verify composite PK and hashed indexes against live DB; measure and report real before/after index size; submit a real end-to-end request to prove the resource_ids_hash filter works against real data; monitor processing-worker/background-worker logs for new errors for a few minutes post-deploy.
